title: Georgia Political Crisis Tracker Update — Sep 13, 2026
summary: Prosecutors arrested United National Movement figure and former interior/defense minister Giorgi Baramidze on Sept. 11 on treason and sabotage charges over remarks about the 1992-93 Abkhazia war, a case opposition allies call the crackdown's furthest reach yet. Three days earlier, 34 countries including every EU member state told the UN Human Rights Council that Georgia's human rights situation continues to deteriorate and demanded the release of arbitrarily detained critics. Civil society figures used the Sept. 12 march marking the movement's 654th consecutive day to announce a push toward a unified opposition coalition. Pardoned Russian activist Denis Kulanin departed Georgia for a third country on Sept. 6 under a five-year re-entry ban, and detained animal-rights campaigner Tamaz Elizbarashvili began a hunger strike on Sept. 8.

title: Georgia Political Crisis Tracker Update — Aug 26, 2026
summary: Prosecutors charged imprisoned former PM Irakli Garibashvili with a new Defense Ministry bribery count carrying 11-15 years, days after he publicly broke with Georgian Dream founder Bidzina Ivanishvili over an earlier plea deal. Eight companies linked to Ivanishvili's Co-Investment Fund were transferred from a Luxembourg holding entity into his wife Ekaterine Khvedelidze's name, which analysts called a possible hedge against future UK sanctions. Tbilisi protesters marked Ukraine's Independence Day with a solidarity march on the movement's 635th consecutive day, and Russian-occupied Tskhinvali registered four candidates for a September 18 'presidential' vote that Georgia does not recognize. Consecutive protest days now exceed 637.
